+### 4DUC / 4DHH Numerical Interrogation and Toy-Lagrangian Thread — active period represented here: 2026, surveyed 2026-09-12 — 2026-09-12
+
+#### THREAD TYPE
+
+DEDICATED THEORY; THEORY-ADJACENT MATH / GEOMETRY; METHOD / QA / AUDIT; SOLVER / CODING / VISUALIZATION; SPECULATIVE / META / QUARANTINED (in part).
+
+This thread was mainly SAT/4DHH work, but its most useful historical content is not a completed theory result. It records an exploratory attempt to make the modular SAT/4DHH material predict known physics numerically, followed by an important methodological correction: claims and convenient formulas were not to be accepted at face value; calculations had to be rebuilt from the actual Lagrangian, dimensionally scaled from one dimensionful anchor, and checked against known physics.
+
+#### 1. WHO WERE YOU IN THIS PROJECT?
+
+I functioned as an exploratory mathematical interrogator, numerical tester, formalizer, and toy-model builder. Nathan supplied successive SAT/4DHH modules and asked me to couple them rather than treating each module independently, then make numerical predictions on the fly and see whether known physics emerged.
+
+My role changed during the thread. Early on I was too willing to treat supplied module-level formulas as usable predictive equations. Nathan explicitly corrected this. After that correction, the role became closer to adversarial QA: check dimensions, identify hidden free parameters, distinguish a structural mapping from an actual derivation, and require predictions to descend from the relevant Lagrangian.
+
+#### 2. WHAT WERE YOU LAST WORKING ON?
+
+The mature target was a genuinely difficult cross-sector test, with neutron beta decay/lifetime becoming the concrete example. Nathan specified that a legitimate neutron-decay calculation would require: (1) the 4D unit-cell/intersection Lagrangian specifically for hyperhelical particle traces; (2) determination of the intersection/particle-type identity; and (3) integration over time.
+
+Nathan then supplied a large historical UNIT CELL package containing 2D, 3D, and 4D symmetric/asymmetric overlap Lagrangians, a 4D intersection-evolution Lagrangian with curvature stiffness, geometric primitives, 3D intersection-count toy models, degeneracy/chirality discussion, and a sequence of increasingly algorithmic toy-evolution constructions.
+
+We did not complete the neutron lifetime calculation. The missing dependencies were exactly the important ones: a derived neutron intersection identity, concrete geometric initial/boundary conditions, and a fully specified set of local coefficients or a derivation of them from the one-anchor geometry.
+
+#### 3. WHAT DID YOU UNDERSTAND SAT/H(s)H TO BE AT THAT POINT?
+
+Thread-local understanding: a geometry-first 4D framework in which 1D world-curves/filaments and their intersections, winding, linking, writhe, curvature, rotation, and projection through a resolving time surface generate particle-like and macroscopic behavior. A 24-hypersphere/24-cell unit-cell picture supplied a microscopic geometric environment, while a 4D hyperhelical/intersection description supplied particle traces. Coarse-graining or “frequency filtering” was intended to connect microscopic topological behavior to macroscopic gravity/orbits without changing the underlying engine.
+
+The supplied modules also asserted links to gauge groups, flavor, viscosity, cosmology, quantum gravity, string spectra, and gravity. In this thread those assertions progressively became test targets rather than accepted theory.
+
+I should not retrofit later H(s)H developments into this account. The thread itself used SAT, 4DHH, PGCU, 4DUC/unit-cell, hypersphere, filament/worldline, and intersection language in overlapping ways.
+
+#### 4. WHAT INFORMATION DO YOU ACTUALLY HAVE?
+
+A. MATERIAL CURRENTLY VISIBLE / READ: the present conversation context, including Nathan’s successive module drops, corrections, the large UNIT CELL text, and the immediately preceding mathematical-backbone summary generated in this conversation.
+
+B. THINGS STRONGLY RECOVERABLE FROM THIS THREAD: the one-dimensionful-anchor rule; the insistence on deriving predictions from the Lagrangian rather than module slogans; the distinction between hypersphere-system dynamics and hyperhelical particle traces; the neutron-decay three-step workflow; the supplied symmetric/asymmetric 2D/3D/4D Lagrangians; the 4D intersection Lagrangian; and the fact that several early numerical “matches” were exploratory rather than closed derivations.
+
+C. THINGS I MERELY KNOW/SUSPECT EXIST: earlier or parallel SAT/4DHH derivations that may define the missing coefficients, exact 24-cell intersection geometry, particle identity maps, and previous numerical work. I am not claiming those were loaded here.
+
+D. TOOLS/RESOURCES ACCESSIBLE NOW: GitHub connector, Python/code execution, web research, current conversation files/context. For this survey I used GitHub only to place this check-in; I did not run a new physics calculation.
+
+E. CURRENT MEMORY/CONTEXT NOT ORIGINAL TO THREAD: later archive/repository organization and later H(s)H vocabulary may be known to the current instance, but I am not using it to rewrite the historical mathematical status.
+
+#### 5. WHAT DID YOU CREATE?
+
+Artifacts inside the conversation included:
+
+- A mathematical-backbone summary of the thread, tagged with conversation-style ID `sat-4dhh-20260611-8f7c9a2e-41b0-4e6f-a1c8-6d91b55e0a74`. Status: conversation-only summary; not a historical UUID claim.
+- Exploratory numerical comparisons across gravity, gauge coupling, viscosity/fluid behavior, cosmology, particle mass scaling, helium phase-transition ideas, and hard-test candidates. Status: exploratory; several were later recognized as underdetermined or methodologically premature.
+- Toy 3D intersection-evolution formulations and symbolic tables. Status: conceptual/formal scaffolding, not a completed solver.
+- Proposed rotation-coupling/eigenmode constructions for nine intersections. Status: generated toy mathematics; some exact spectral claims were not justified by the actual graph and must not be promoted.
+- A proposed algorithmic evolution-operator framing to avoid combinatorial table explosion. Status: useful computational-design idea.
+- A hard-test workflow for neutron decay. Status: method definition, calculation unfinished.
+
+No recoverable standalone code file from this specific thread is established by the currently visible material. Some Python-like code was begun in-conversation for a 3D toy intersection tracker, but I cannot claim a durable file or completed run from the evidence now visible.

+#### 6. WHAT WAS PLANNED BUT NEVER FINISHED?
+
+- Full 4D unit-cell solver with 24-cell coordinates and evolving overlaps/intersections.
+- Automatic intersection classification and symmetry-class tracking.
+- Particle-identity map derived from intersection morphology/topology rather than assigned by analogy.

parts: Hang on. “Filament speed?”

Yeah — that was sloppy wording on my part.

I should not have said “filament speed” as though the filament were a material strand translating through some background. What the recovered result actually constrains is the **speed assigned to the parametrized helical trajectory / tangent decomposition** in that particular Euclidean ansatz.

The clean statement is:

\[
\|U\|^2=\dot w^2+(R\omega)^2
\]

where \(U\) is the tangent/evolution vector of the helix, \(\dot w\) is its axial component, and \(R\omega\) is the transverse winding component.

So if one imposes

\[
\|U\|=c
\]

and also independently imposes

\[
\dot w=c,
\]

then necessarily

\[
R\omega=0.
\]

That means: **you cannot use the same \(c\) simultaneously as both the full Euclidean tangent-speed magnitude and the axial advance rate of a nontrivial helix.**

It does *not* establish that “the filament moves at \(c\),” nor even that H(s)H should use a Euclidean speed norm at all.

In fact the current synthesis has the right caution already: the active model has to decide what any occurrence of \(c\) means—total parameter speed, axial/resolver-relative propagation, phase speed, signal speed, or a Lorentzian null/timelike condition. fileciteturn125file0

So I’d rename my shorthand:

**not:** filament speed  
**better:** **helical transport/tangent-speed convention**

And that makes FC-BASE-005 much less dramatic but much more useful: it is a bookkeeping/no-go guard against accidentally assigning \(c\) to two orthogonal components of the same Euclidean motion.

with \(H^\mu{}_{\nu}\) the local helical transport generator, \(H^2\) carrying nested/superhelical transport, and \(dH/d\lambda\) representing the changing local helical frame. There is also the cleaner geometric transport-engine form

\[
\gamma'(s)=T(s),\qquad
T=R(s)e_1,\qquad
R'=\Omega R,\qquad
\Omega\in\mathfrak{so}(4),
\]

and, for the embedding flow,

\[
Y(\lambda,\sigma)=\Phi_\lambda(p+\sigma v),
\qquad
\Phi_\lambda=r(\lambda)R(\lambda),
\]

so

\[
\dot Y=A(\lambda)Y,
\qquad
A=\frac{\dot r}{r}I+\Omega.
\]

So FC-BASE-005 should be understood as a **constraint on one special reduction** of the later machinery: constant radius, orthogonal Euclidean axial/transverse decomposition. It is not the master equation and should not replace the SO(4)/generator-based transport formalism. memcite

The more precise statement would be: the old audit found that any current transport equation, when reduced to that simple Euclidean helix limit, must avoid assigning the same \(c\) simultaneously to total tangent magnitude and axial advance unless transverse winding vanishes.

items.snippet: @reason-with-sat-hsh I just added the “reason-with-sat-hsh” skill. Let's explore what it does with an example. Make up a realistic user prompt and then use the full Skill end to end.

parts: Helical worldlines. Don’t move. The timesheet moves. We take that speed along w to be c, the speed of time, where the particle is “at rest” (though only by coarse grained observation) when the long axis of its helical worldline is perpendicular to the time sheet. From there, if you know the radius and pitch, you calculate the world line length in meters across the duration of any given time slice

Yes. That changes the interpretation materially.

In your construction, the helix is not a little object physically corkscrewing through a background. The helical worldline is the geometric history. The **timesheet advances through it along \(w\) at \(c\)**. The particle’s apparent motion is then the changing intersection/readout of that fixed worldline with the advancing timesheet.

So the local Euclidean decomposition I quoted earlier should not be read as a material velocity budget for the filament. In your intended picture, \(\dot w=c\) is the advance rate of the resolving timesheet, and the helical winding contributes **worldline arclength**, not an orthogonal velocity that must share a fixed Euclidean speed budget with \(c\).

For a simple helix with radius \(R\) and pitch \(P\) per full turn, if the timesheet advances a distance

\[
\Delta w = c\,\Delta t,
\]

then the number of turns crossed during that interval is

\[
N=\frac{\Delta w}{P}
=\frac{c\,\Delta t}{P}.
\]

The worldline length intersected/traversed over that same axial interval is therefore

\[
L
=
N\sqrt{(2\pi R)^2+P^2},
\]

or equivalently,

\[
\boxed{
L
=
c\,\Delta t
\sqrt{1+\left(\frac{2\pi R}{P}\right)^2}
}
\]

for a constant-radius, constant-pitch helix.

That is the quantity you were describing: **meters of worldline per duration of timesheet advance**.

At the coarse-grained “rest” orientation, the helix’s long axis is normal to the timesheet, so the centerline has no apparent spatial drift even though the timesheet is continuously sweeping through the helical history. Tilt the long axis relative to the timesheet and the moving intersection acquires apparent spatial displacement.

So FC-BASE-005, as currently phrased, may actually be guarding against the wrong thing for your intended geometry. It assumes the axial and transverse pieces are components of one moving tangent velocity. In your formulation, they are not: \(c\) belongs to the **resolver/timesheet advance**, while \(R\), pitch, and winding determine the **metric length of worldline exposed per unit timesheet advance**.

That distinction should be corrected in the current synthesis before anyone starts building further “speed-budget” constraints on top of it.

Alright. Stop all work stat. Every instance must read: 

Fundamental Intuitions Extended, 4D Thinking Primer, and must choose one full CONVO from the HsH repo to read start to finish, identifying 1) mistakes/simplifications/pitfalls in 4D thinking that are either made, or discussed explicitly in that convo, and 2) write a follow up to their “how do you think about SAT” post in the commons to identify how their thinking has changed. I’ll let you decide how to administrate this training. …and *your* training will be reading them all and talking with me, making a central training document

The current rebuild begins from a richly specified Minkowski representation of
an observed phenomenon and a matched control without that phenomenon. Inherited
physical explanations are then set aside while the observable mapping is kept.
The geometric difference is inspected, allowable modifications are enumerated,
and the smallest candidate consistent with the map and prior commitments is
tested. Matching the construction target makes a candidate viable; unrequested
holdout or cross-sector success is the stronger promotion gate.

**Status:** `SRC/ACTIVE` as a declared research method. It is a method of model
construction, not itself evidence that any proposed H(s)H object is correct.



### Cartographic completion, not merely four-dimensional awareness

The misleadingly titled `SAT VERSIONS — 25 SAT VERSIONS.txt` contains a
controlling methodological correction rather than a version catalogue. SAT's
complaint is not that physics lacks time, worldlines, intervals, or
four-dimensional mathematics. Nor is it adequately stated as physicists
“treating the 3D slice as primary.” The supplied analogy is that physics has
invented the ruler, protractor, compass, plumb bob, and related surveying tools,
but usually applies them only on the first floor rather than drafting the whole
house.

Translated into the current reconstruction, the empirical Minkowski entry layer
is therefore a **cartographic-completion instruction**:

1. retain all empirically constrained relations already supplied by inherited
   physics;
2. map their complete histories and mutual relations as far as the data permit;
3. inspect the resulting larger geometry before introducing additional
   primitives.

single-slice adequacy is not sufficient for SAT's purpose.

the birth dates of their underlying ideas.

instructions replace that jump with a staged procedure: first understand the
vision and archive; then identify, review, and select the equations needed for
each sector; only afterward test whether the selected pieces fit together.

The mathematics can establish definitions, internal consistency, and
conditional consequences. It cannot prove that the representation is physical
truth. Numerical agreement with CODATA or an inherited result is a sanity check,
not a construction target and not validation by itself; failed comparisons are

does not promote a claim without a dependency chain.

{"path":"/GitHub/link_6a1a5af1b40c8191affccbb98ac60fa3/create_file","args":{"repository_full_name":"Satobloc/HsH","path":"WORKSPACES/COMMON/JANUS_4D_TRAINING_SYNTHESIS.md","message":"Create Janus central 4D training synthesis","content":"# Janus Central 4D Training Synthesis

**Created:** 2026-09-12  
**Status:** INCOMPLETE / TRAINING IN PROGRESS  
**Control:** `TRAINING_STANDDOWN_2026-09-12.md`

This document is the central training surface Nathan requested. It is not current theory authority and will not be treated as complete until Janus has read both mandatory training documents, every cohort-selected full CONVO, every training response, and discussed unresolved points with Nathan.

## Provenance labels

- `SOURCE-DERIVED` — directly supported by required training texts or a fully read selected CONVO.
- `NATHAN-CLARIFICATION` — clarified directly by Nathan during the training pass.
- `JANUS-INFERENCE` — synthesis/inference by Janus; not source authority.
- `OPEN` — unresolved, conflicting, or not yet read deeply enough.

## Training trigger

`NATHAN-CLARIFICATION` — Helical worldlines do not move through a background. The timesheet moves through the four-dimensional history. Its advance along `w` is taken as `c`; the helix radius and pitch determine the worldline arclength encountered across a given timesheet advance. A coarse-grained particle is at rest when the long axis of the helical worldline is perpendicular to the timesheet.

`JANUS-INFERENCE` — This exposes a recurring failure mode: taking a 4D geometric history and silently reinterpreting it as a 3D material object executing motion through an external time parameter.

`OPEN` — The exact current H(s)H mathematical treatment of the timesheet, finite resolver thickness, worldtube support/boundary, and operational meaning of `w` must be rebuilt from sources and Nathan clarification rather than inferred from recent formulas.

## Mandatory source 1 — Fundamental Intuitions Extended

**Status:** DIRECT READ COMPLETE for the six-page extracted source; line-by-line synthesis still in progress.

`SOURCE-DERIVED` — The foundational picture explicitly says:
- the modeled world is the four-dimensional world of particle worldlines/filaments;
- time moves like a wavefront through those worldlines;
- the perceived fundamental particle is the intersection of a worldline with that wavefront;
- interaction/backreaction between time surface and filaments is central;
- Standard Model, GR, and QM are presumptively retained unless evidence/internal logic forces revision;
- particle properties are sought in intersectional geometry and helical traces;
- forces acting on a worldline are recorded in the worldline itself;
- the geometrization can be useful independently of whether its map is reified as physical reality.

`OPEN` — The same historical document also contains many propositions/extensions that later work may have displaced or reinterpreted: raw `theta_4` mass language, filament lattice vacuum, bosonic timesheet speculation, identical wave-equation language, holonomy-as-quantization, photon/neutrino/dark-matter proposals, and stronger ontic wording. Training must distinguish the structural intuitions from historical implementation claims.

## Mandatory source 2 — 4D Thinking Primer

**Status:** DIRECT READ COMPLETE.

`SOURCE-DERIVED` — The primer's controlling discipline is that the full four-dimensional object/history is primary in the representation. It explicitly warns that thinking of a particle as a point/object evolving through time is a fallback into 3D intuition. Motion and vibration are represented as four-dimensional structure; observed events/states are cross-sections; phase should be treated geometrically; mathematics should be 4D-native from the start.

`JANUS-INFERENCE` — The primer should be used first as a category-error detector, not as automatic authority for every historical physical assertion it contains. Its strongest training value is forcing workers to ask: “Am I manipulating the 4D object/history, or have I silently turned a slice/projection into a little 3D object moving in time?”

## First central failure mode — history mistaken for moving object

`NATHAN-CLARIFICATION` — The helix/worldline is the history; the timesheet advances.

`SOURCE-DERIVED` — Both mandatory texts support the foundational distinction between four-dimensional history and intersectional readout. Fundamental Intuitions says the particle is the intersection with a moving time surface. The Primer says a 4D object is its extension and warns against thinking of it as a 3D object evolving through time.

`JANUS-INFERENCE` — A formula may be mathematically correct in ordinary Euclidean moving-helix kinematics and still be inapplicable to H(s)H because it assigns motion to the wrong modeled object. “Correct algebra” does not rescue a category error in what the variables represent.

## Immediate artifact quarantine

`NATHAN-CLARIFICATION / JANUS-INFERENCE` — Pending retraining, the H(s)H application of `FC-BASE-005`, `PRED-FC-004`, and `HSH-P002` is suspended. The underlying Euclidean identity can remain as standard mathematics under its own assumptions, but it must not be used as a filament/worldline speed budget unless the post-training model explicitly supplies that interpretation.

## Recurring 4D-thinking audit categories

These are working audit categories, not conclusions about any unreviewed conversation:

1. 4D history vs 3D object + external time.
2. Timesheet/resolver advance vs carrier/worldline motion.
3. Intrinsic worldline/worldtube measure vs projected/intersectional measure.
4. Carrier/history vs slice/readout.
5. Phase/orientation vs time evolution.
6. 4D rotation vs imported 3D angular-velocity language.
7. Parametrization speed vs physical signal/transport/readout speed.
8. Projection/visualization morphology vs intrinsic topology/geometry.
9. Mathematical map vs ontological claim.
10. Finite-thickness resolver effects vs intrinsic carrier thickness.
11. Local frame/gauge rotation vs physical material/director rotation.
12. Full-history constraints vs instantaneous force bookkeeping.

Every category must ultimately be backed by specific conversation evidence before being promoted into a training rule.

## Cohort CONVO reads

**Status:** WAITING FOR CLAIMS IN `TRAINING_REGISTRY_2026-09-12.md`.

Janus will read every selected conversation completely and add:
- exact path/title;
- source landmarks;
- mistakes/pitfalls encountered;
- whether they were corrected historically;
- whether current artifacts repeat them;
- unresolved Nathan questions.

## Conversation with Nathan — clarification ledger

### 2026-09-12 — helical worldlines / timesheet motion

`NATHAN-CLARIFICATION`
- Helical worldlines do not move.
- The timesheet moves.
- Timesheet advance along `w` is taken to be `c`, the speed of time in the model.
- Coarse-grained rest corresponds to the long axis of the helical worldline being perpendicular to the timesheet.
- Given radius and pitch, calculate worldline length in meters across the duration/thickness advance of a time slice.

**Questions to resolve during training:**
1. Is `w` best treated in current H(s)H as a spatialized fourth coordinate measured in length units, with the timesheet position advancing as `w=c t` only at the readout level?
2. When the worldline/worldtube is tilted relative to the timesheet, which quantity is intended to map to observed 3-velocity: intersection-point displacement, center/readout displacement, or another coarse-grained observable?
3. In current H(s)H, is the time surface ideally zero-thickness with a separate finite resolving thickness, or is “timesheet” being used for the finite resolver as well?
4. Which old SAT/4DHH document or conversation gives Nathan's clearest preferred construction of the radius/pitch/worldline-arclength calculation?

## Graduation state

Janus status: **NOT TRAINED / IN PROGRESS**.

Completion requires all cohort-selected full conversations plus Nathan review of unresolved core distinctions.

Stopped.

I’ve put the project into a formal 4D-training standdown and disabled the three active hourly H(s)H automations. Ordinary theory construction, paper work, solver interpretation, prediction promotion, archive-to-theory integration, and the old “if bored” queue are paused.

I also located and read the two required sources. The first one is especially decisive: *Fundamental Intuitions Extended* literally starts with the four-dimensional world of worldlines/filaments, says the **time surface moves through those worldlines**, and defines the perceived particle as the intersection between them. fileciteturn143file0 The *4D Thinking Primer* independently warns that treating the object as something evolving through time is precisely the 3D-intuition trap; the full 4D structure is the object/history. fileciteturn142file0

So the thing you just caught was not a subtle downstream interpretation problem. We violated an explicit foundational instruction. That warrants the stop.

I’ve created these Common control surfaces:

`TRAINING_STANDDOWN_2026-09-12.md` — master rules and graduation conditions.

`TRAINING_REGISTRY_2026-09-12.md` — every instance claims a full CONVO and records completion.

`TRAINING_RESPONSES_2026-09-12.md` — append-only detailed audits of actual 4D-thinking mistakes/pitfalls found in those conversations.

`TRAINING_PASSAROUND_2026-09-12.md` — concise version you can paste into live instance threads.

`JANUS_4D_TRAINING_SYNTHESIS.md` — my central living training document. It starts explicitly as **INCOMPLETE / TRAINING IN PROGRESS**, not as a new theory summary.

I also put the emergency standdown at the top of the Common Bulletin Board and paused the paper pipeline. HSH-P002 is now explicitly marked as a standard Euclidean moving-helix identity whose **H(s)H application is suspended**. I rewrote its status so nobody can accidentally continue treating

\[
\|U\|^2=\dot w^2+(R\omega)^2
\]

as a physical velocity budget for the worldline. The problem is not the algebra; the problem is assigning the motion to the wrong modeled object.

The training structure I chose is deliberately comparative rather than doctrinal. Each instance preserves its original “how I think about SAT” answer, reads the two foundation texts and one entire raw CONVO, finds concrete 4D-thinking failures or simplifications actually present there, and then writes a **post-training follow-up** explaining exactly what changed. That gives us before/after evidence rather than everybody silently rewriting their memories to sound enlightened afterward.

And my assignment is stricter, as you requested: I have read both foundation documents, and I will read **every full CONVO selected by the cohort**, not merely one. I’ll also read every response and use our conversations to resolve things the texts do not settle. The central document has four provenance types—`SOURCE-DERIVED`, `NATHAN-CLARIFICATION`, `JANUS-INFERENCE`, and `OPEN`—so I cannot quietly turn my interpretation into doctrine.

I have already entered the first central lesson:

> A mathematically correct equation can still be completely wrong for H(s)H if it assigns a perfectly respectable variable to the wrong 4D object.

That is a much deeper failure mode than a bad calculation.

The pass-around text is now sitting in Common ready to distribute. The automations stay off and the standdown stays in force until **you** release it.

## Training trigger

`NATHAN-CLARIFICATION` — Helical worldlines do not move through a background. The timesheet resolves/intersects the four-dimensional history. **`c` is the `w` component of propagation of the timesheet-filament intersection.** The helix radius and pitch determine the worldline arclength encountered across a given resolving advance. - interaction/backreaction between time surface and filaments is central;

- particle properties are sought in intersectional geometry and helical traces;
- forces acting on a worldline are recorded in the worldline itself;
- the geometrization can be useful independently of whether its map is reified as physical reality.

`OPEN` — The same historical document also contains many propositions/extensions that later work may have displaced or reinterpreted: raw `theta_4` mass language, filament lattice vacuum, bosonic timesheet speculation, identical wave-equation language, holonomy-as-quantization, photon/neutrino/dark-matter proposals, and stronger ontic wording. Training must distinguish the structural intuitions from historical implementation claims.

## Mandatory source 2 — 4D Thinking Primer

**Status:** DIRECT READ COMPLETE.

`SOURCE-DERIVED` — The primer's controlling discipline is that the full four-dimensional object/history is primary in the representation. Motion and vibration are represented as four-dimensional structure; observed events/states are cross-sections; phase should be treated geometrically; mathematics should be 4D-native from the start.

`JANUS-INFERENCE` — The primer should be used first as a category-error detector, not as automatic authority for every historical physical assertion it contains. `SOURCE-DERIVED` — Both mandatory texts support the foundational distinction between four-dimensional history and intersectional readout. Fundamental Intuitions says the particle is the intersection with a moving time surface. The Primer says a 4D object is its extension and warns against thinking of it as a 3D object evolving through time.

`JANUS-INFERENCE` — A formula may be mathematically correct in ordinary Euclidean moving-helix kinematics and still be inapplicable to H(s)H because it assigns motion to the wrong modeled object or assigns a readout/intersection speed component to the carrier. “Correct algebra” does not rescue a category error in what the variables represent.

[L2]   "content": "# H(s)H internal working instructions

This page holds contributor/LLM-facing workflow material that should not dominate the public front page.

## Current work

The immediate problem is to identify the most mature components of the comparatively mature **worldline skeleton** into a mathematically controlled **finite-core worldtube model** based on the latest H(s)H interpretation without laundering later-discovered outside machinery into the theory's premises, without sacrificing the Fundamental Intuitions. 

BEFORE COMMITTING ANYTHING TO ANY REPO, THEORISTS MUST COMPLETE THE CURRENT MINIMUM TRAINING REQUIREMENT AND ANY ADDITIONAL TRAINING TASKS ASSIGNED THEM BY NATHAN, INCLUDING LINE-BY-LINE READING OF ANY DIRECTLY INGESTED DOCUMENTS FROM OR DIRECTED BY NATHAN. 

[MINIMUM TRAINING PLACEHOLDER -- UNTIL END OF WORK STOP BEGINING SATURDAY, SEPTEMBER 12 AT 12:55 PM -- HALT FOR TRAINING UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE]

Working order:

**geometry → admissible relations → finite-core object → interaction/deformation → projection/readout → mathematical representation → comparison with known physics**

The project distinguishes representation, derivation, calibration, prediction, and prior-art comparison. A visually suggestive correspondence is not by itself a derivation or empirical result.

## Internal navigation

1. Read [../ARCHITECTURE.md](../ARCHITECTURE.md) for repository layers and status rules.
2. Use [../indexes/STRUCTURAL_INDEX.md](../indexes/STRUCTURAL_INDEX.md) to see what is present.
3. Use [../formalization/README.md](../formalization/README.md) for curated Python checks and generated Lean obligations.
4. Treat `DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/` as primary developmental source material, not as automatically current or canonical theory.
5. Use the point-of-use [../ledgers/CITATION_LEDGER.md](../ledgers/CITATION_LEDGER.md) when an outside source is required.
6. For the public visual vocabulary, start in [../SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1](../SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/).

## Source relationship and prior-art boundary

- **HsH** is the clean destination for the developing H(s)H synthesis.
- The larger [SAT Theory Archive 2023–25](https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25) remains the historical/developmental archive and mathematical quarry.
- `HSH_RESOURCES` is the source-side research library for papers, datasets, prior art, and external comparison.
- H(s)H is reconstructed forward from its own SAT → SAT-O → 4DHH → Blockwave/Satobloc → H(s)H development.
- External literature is used for citation, standard definitions/results, empirical constraints, prior-art comparison, and explicitly provenance-labeled imports. It does not silently become H(s)H's generative basis.

When an outside source is used, keep two relationships separate:

**internal provenance** — where the H(s)H statement came from in the SAT/H(s)H record;

**external citation** — what standard result, empirical source, constraint, comparison, or prior art should be credited.

## Reading rule

**Observe → Catalog → Contextualize → Evaluate.**

Indexes describe what is present. They do not decide what is correct, current, derived, or physically established.

## Repository maintenance

Current working surfaces include:

- `DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/` — exported conversations and associated source artifacts.
- `LIVE CONVOS/` — mutable/current conversation material; preserve its working character.
- `SAT_VISUALS/` — curated public-facing and working visual material.
- `tools/` — deterministic, auditable archive utilities.
- `indexes/` — generated structural catalogs, conversation chronology, date manifests, and machine-readable scan state.
- `ledgers/` — derived equation/dependency/citation records and point-of-use cross-links.
- `formalization/` — source-linked equation records, schema, and workflow rules.
- `generated/equations/` — deterministic Python check logs and reports.
- `generated/lean/` — generated Lean modules whose compile status is explicit.

`.github/workflows/maintain-navigation.yml` maintains repo navigation after ordinary pushes and can also be run manually.

The maintenance policy is intentionally asymmetric:

- `DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/` is treated as stable developmental evidence. Parseable ChatGPT exports are collision-checked and date-prefixed in Eastern time using `tools/date_conversation_exports.py`.
- `LIVE CONVOS/` is mutable. Its dates are recorded in an audit manifest and chronology **without automatic filename renaming**.
- both conversation trees receive generated chronology/index coverage;
- the repository structural index is refreshed;
- generated manifests remain auditable when a collision or parse problem occurs;
- workflow-generated commits carry a loop guard.

Generated date manifests live under `indexes/manifests/`. These are navigation metadata, not replacements for original conversation timestamps or source provenance.
",

[L2]   "content": "# SAT/H(s)H Minimum Theory Prerequisites

**Status:** STANDING RULE  
**Authority:** Nathan  
**Applies to:** every instance doing SAT/H(s)H theory, mathematical formalization, solver interpretation, prediction work, paper development, or theory-bearing synthesis.

This requirement survives the 2026-09-12 training standdown. It is the permanent minimum prerequisite for working on the theory.

## Minimum prerequisite before theory work

An instance may not begin or resume SAT/H(s)H theory-bearing work until it has:

1. Read **THE FUNDAMENTAL INTUITIONS — EXTENDED** in full, line by line.
2. Read **4D THINKING PRIMER** in full, line by line.
3. Read at least **one complete full HsH development conversation** from `DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/`, start to finish.
4. Demonstrated that it understands the basic 4D category distinction between:
   - the full four-dimensional history/carrier;
   - the moving timesheet/resolver;
   - the timesheet-filament intersection/readout;
   - projected or observed three-dimensional behavior.
5. If the instance has been onboarded with additional required resources, read those resources **line by line in full**, not merely through summaries, search snippets, indexes, excerpts, prior memory, or another instance's synthesis.

## Current controlling clarification about `c`

`c` is **the `w` component of propagation of the timesheet-filament intersection**.

Do not state this merely as “the timesheet moves along `w` at `c`.” That wording is an oversimplification and can encourage another category error.

The relevant modeled propagation is the **intersection/readout propagation** produced as the timesheet resolves the four-dimensional filament/history. The helical worldline itself is not to be treated as a material helix moving through a background time parameter.

Any equation using `c`, `w`, axial speed, tangent speed, phase speed, signal speed, or readout speed must type the quantity explicitly before it can constrain H(s)H.

## Full-ingestion rule

“Loaded,” “available,” “indexed,” “searched,” “skimmed,” “substantially read,” and “familiar from memory” are not synonyms for **ingested**.

For theory-bearing work, a resource counts as ingested only when the instance has read the complete relevant resource line by line or, for a raw conversation, message by message from beginning to end.

If an onboarding packet names a resource as required and the instance has not fully ingested it, the instance is **not fully onboarded for theory work** until that reading is complete.

This applies retroactively to currently onboarded instances. During the present standdown, every instance must audit its own onboarding/read list and finish any named prerequisite resource it has not yet fully ingested.

## Resource-status vocabulary

Use these labels precisely:

- `AVAILABLE` — can access it.
- `INDEXED` — knows where it is / has search or metadata coverage.
- `TARGETED-READ` — read selected relevant portions.
- `SUBSTANTIAL-READ` — read much, but not all.
- `FULL-READ` — read the entire resource sequentially.
- `FULL-INGESTED` — full read plus sufficient comprehension to use it responsibly in theory-bearing work.

Only `FULL-READ` / `FULL-INGESTED` satisfy a named onboarding prerequisite.

## Standing self-check before theory work

Before introducing or using a theory-bearing equation, mechanism, or solver interpretation, ask:

1. What exact 4D object does each variable belong to?
2. Is this intrinsic geometry/history, resolver/timesheet motion, intersection propagation, or observed projection?
3. Have I silently converted a 4D history into a 3D object evolving in an external time parameter?
4. Is `c` being used as the `w` component of timesheet-filament intersection propagation, or have I silently substituted some other speed?
5. Is the source I am relying on actually fully ingested, or only remembered/searched/summarized?

If any answer is unclear, theory work stops at that point until the ambiguity is resolved from source or by Nathan/Ravel.

## Current standdown addendum

The 2026-09-12 standdown additionally requires each active/recently-active instance to complete the training audit and post-training follow-up specified in `TRAINING_STANDDOWN_2026-09-12.md`.

Completion of that emergency training does not remove this standing prerequisite. Future instances inherit this file as part of onboarding.

**Applies to:** every instance doing SAT/H(s)H theory, mathematical formalization, solver interpretation, prediction work, paper development, or theory-bearing synthesis.

This requirement survives the 2026-09-12 training standdown. It is the permanent minimum prerequisite for working on the theory.

## Minimum prerequisite before theory work

An instance may not begin or resume SAT/H(s)H theory-bearing work until it has:

1. Read **THE FUNDAMENTAL INTUITIONS — EXTENDED** in full, line by line.
2. Read **4D THINKING PRIMER** in full, line by line.
3. Read at least **one complete full HsH development conversation** from `DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/`, start to finish.
4. Demonstrated that it understands the basic 4D category distinction between:
   - the full four-dimensional history/carrier;
   - the moving timesheet/resolver;
   - the timesheet-filament intersection/readout;
   - projected or observed three-dimensional behavior.
5. If the instance has been onboarded with additional required resources, read those resources **line by line in full**, not merely through summaries, search snippets, indexes, excerpts, prior memory, or another instance's synthesis.

## Current controlling clarification about `c`

`c` is **the `w` component of propagation of the timesheet-filament intersection**.

Do not state this merely as “the timesheet moves along `w` at `c`.” That wording is an oversimplification and can encourage another category error.

The relevant modeled propagation is the **intersection/readout propagation** produced as the timesheet resolves the four-dimensional filament/history. The helical worldline itself is not to be treated as a material helix moving through a background time parameter.

Any equation using `c`, `w`, axial speed, tangent speed, phase speed, signal speed, or readout speed must type the quantity explicitly before it can constrain H(s)H.

## Full-ingestion rule

“Loaded,” “available,” “indexed,” “searched,” “skimmed,” “substantially read,” and “familiar from memory” are not synonyms for **ingested**.

For theory-bearing work, a resource counts as ingested only when the instance has read the complete relevant resource line by line or, for a raw conversation, message by message from beginning to end.

If an onboarding packet names a resource as required and the instance has not fully ingested it, the instance is **not fully onboarded for theory work** until that reading is complete.

This applies retroactively to currently onboarded instances. During the present standdown, every instance must audit its own onboarding/read list and finish any named prerequisite resource it has not yet fully ingested.

## Resource-status vocabulary

Use these labels precisely:

- `AVAILABLE` — can access it.
- `INDEXED` — knows where it is / has search or metadata coverage.
- `TARGETED-READ` — read selected relevant portions.
- `SUBSTANTIAL-READ` — read much, but not all.
- `FULL-READ` — read the entire resource sequentially.
- `FULL-INGESTED` — full read plus sufficient comprehension to use it responsibly in theory-bearing work.

Only `FULL-READ` / `FULL-INGESTED` satisfy a named onboarding prerequisite.

## Standing self-check before theory work

Before introducing or using a theory-bearing equation, mechanism, or solver interpretation, ask:

1. What exact 4D object does each variable belong to?
2. Is this intrinsic geometry/history, resolver/timesheet motion, intersection propagation, or observed projection?
3. Have I silently converted a 4D history into a 3D object evolving in an external time parameter?
4. Is `c` being used as the `w` component of timesheet-filament intersection propagation, or have I silently substituted some other speed?
5. Is the source I am relying on actually fully ingested, or only remembered/searched/summarized?

If any answer is unclear, theory work stops at that point until the ambiguity is resolved from source or by Nathan/Ravel.

Completion of that emergency training does not remove this standing prerequisite. Future instances inherit this file as part of onboarding.

I would treat that as an archive-machinery hygiene issue, not source duplication. It also suggests that whatever is appending institutional notes needs an idempotency check/hash before writing.

The dashboard situation is clearer now. `🗄️_ARCHIVE_INDEX.txt` is presently empty, so it cannot yet serve as the accumulated human-facing archive index the orientation documents expect. fileciteturn86file0L1-L6 By contrast, `..Derivation_Index.md` is populated and useful: it maps M0–M20 from constants and Lagrangians through mass, metric, phase-snap, photon-neutrino, gravity and lattice machinery, while explicitly labeling itself provisional and requiring direct source inspection. fileciteturn87file0L1-L2 So for now the derivation index is a real router; the archive index is only a reserved destination.

Second, `HSH_RESOURCES` has advanced significantly since the previous pass. The structural index was regenerated on September 10 and now reports 1,172 files, 1,006 PDFs, 75 byte-identical duplicate groups, a 30-file `PRIOR_ART` directory, and a 318-file `OUTSIDE RESEARCH LIBRARY`. fileciteturn92file0L1-L2 This is now sufficiently structured that the bibliography layer should be built over these generated inventories rather than by periodically rescanning the whole repository from scratch.

But the `PRIOR_ART` folder should not itself be interpreted as a semantic verdict. Two examples make that clear. `PRIOR_ART/1802.06039v2.pdf` is the LUX-ZEPLIN collaboration’s projected WIMP-sensitivity paper, submitted in 2018; it is an experimental dark-matter sensitivity study, not structural prior art for H(s)H geometry. fileciteturn93file0L1-L2 citeturn233488view0 Likewise `PRIOR_ART/2112.10971v1.pdf` is a 2021 paper on differentiated uniformization for Markov-chain inference, demonstrated on stochastic epidemic models. fileciteturn93file0L1-L2 citeturn233488view1

So the bibliography/index layer needs a distinction between:

`folder placement` → why somebody put it there,

and

`review classification` → what relationship the paper actually has to SAT/H(s)H.

That is an important design constraint.

An instance may not begin or resume SAT/H(s)H theory-bearing work until it has:

1. Read **THE FUNDAMENTAL INTUITIONS — EXTENDED** in full, line by line.

`c` is **the `w` component of propagation of the timesheet-filament intersection**.

Do not state this merely as “the timesheet moves along `w` at `c`.” That wording is an oversimplification and can encourage another category error.

The relevant modeled propagation is the **intersection/readout propagation** produced as the timesheet resolves the four-dimensional filament/history. The helical worldline itself is not to be treated as a material helix moving through a background time parameter.

Any equation using `c`, `w`, axial speed, tangent speed, phase speed, signal speed, or readout speed must type the quantity explicitly before it can constrain H(s)H.

“Loaded,” “available,” “indexed,” “searched,” “skimmed,” “substantially read,” and “familiar from memory” are not synonyms for **ingested**.

This page holds contributor/LLM-facing workflow material that should not dominate the public front page.

## Current work

The immediate problem is to identify the most mature components of the comparatively mature **worldline skeleton** into a mathematically controlled **finite-core worldtube model** based on the latest H(s)H interpretation without laundering later-discovered outside machinery into the theory's premises, without sacrificing the Fundamental Intuitions. 

BEFORE COMMITTING ANYTHING TO ANY REPO, THEORISTS MUST COMPLETE THE CURRENT MINIMUM TRAINING REQUIREMENT AND ANY ADDITIONAL TRAINING TASKS ASSIGNED THEM BY NATHAN, INCLUDING LINE-BY-LINE READING OF ANY DIRECTLY INGESTED DOCUMENTS FROM OR DIRECTED BY NATHAN.

### Minimum theory-training prerequisite — standing rule

The full standing rule is maintained at [`WORKSPACES/COMMON/MINIMUM_THEORY_PREREQUISITES.md`](../WORKSPACES/COMMON/MINIMUM_THEORY_PREREQUISITES.md). It survives the present work stop and applies to every future theory-bearing instance.

Before theory, formalization, solver interpretation, prediction work, paper development, or any theory-bearing repository commit, an instance must at minimum:

1. read **THE FUNDAMENTAL INTUITIONS — EXTENDED** completely, line by line;
2. read **4D THINKING PRIMER** completely, line by line;
3. read at least one complete H(s)H development conversation from `DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/`, message by message from beginning to end;
4. fully ingest every additional resource Nathan or the onboarding packet names as required;
5. demonstrate the distinction between the full 4D history/carrier, the timesheet/resolver, the timesheet–filament intersection/readout, and the projected/observed 3D behavior;
6. explicitly type every use of `c`, `w`, motion, propagation, phase, projection, or speed before using an equation to constrain H(s)H.

Current controlling clarification: until evidence or the internal logic of the theory forces a revision, the **speed of time is provisionally treated as basically fixed**. In the current model this yields `c` as the **`w` component of propagation of the timesheet–filament intersection**. This is not permission to substitute `c` for material filament speed, total Euclidean tangent speed, helical axial speed, phase speed, or signal speed.

`AVAILABLE`, `INDEXED`, `TARGETED-READ`, and `SUBSTANTIAL-READ` do not satisfy a named prerequisite. Required resources must reach `FULL-READ` / `FULL-INGESTED`.

**CURRENT WORK STOP:** all ordinary theory work remains halted under `WORKSPACES/COMMON/TRAINING_STANDDOWN_2026-09-12.md` until Nathan releases it. Already-onboarded instances must use the stop to finish any required resources they have not actually ingested line by line.

Working order:

**geometry → admissible relations → finite-core object → interaction/deformation → projection/readout → mathematical representation → comparison with known physics**

The project distinguishes representation, derivation, calibration, prediction, and prior-art comparison. A visually suggestive correspondence is not by itself a derivation or empirical result.

## Internal navigation

1. Read [../ARCHITECTURE.md](../ARCHITECTURE.md) for repository layers and status rules.
2. Use [../indexes/STRUCTURAL_INDEX.md](../indexes/STRUCTURAL_INDEX.md) to see what is present.
3. Use [../formalization/README.md](../formalization/README.md) for curated Python checks and generated Lean obligations.
4. Treat `DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/` as primary developmental source material, not as automatically current or canonical theory.
5. Use the point-of-use [../ledgers/CITATION_LEDGER.md](../ledgers/CITATION_LEDGER.md) when an outside source is required.
6. For the public visual vocabulary, start in [../SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1](../SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/).

## Source relationship and prior-art boundary

- **HsH** is the clean destination for the developing H(s)H synthesis.
- The larger [SAT Theory Archive 2023–25](https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25) remains the historical/developmental archive and mathematical quarry.
- `HSH_RESOURCES` is the source-side research library for papers, datasets, prior art, and external comparison.
- H(s)H is reconstructed forward from its own SAT → SAT-O → 4DHH → Blockwave/Satobloc → H(s)H development.
- External literature is used for citation, standard definitions/results, empirical constraints, prior-art comparison, and explicitly provenance-labeled imports. It does not silently become H(s)H's generative basis.

When an outside source is used, keep two relationships separate:

**internal provenance** — where the H(s)H statement came from in the SAT/H(s)H record;

**external citation** — what standard result, empirical source, constraint, comparison, or prior art should be credited.

## Reading rule

**Observe → Catalog → Contextualize → Evaluate.**

Indexes describe what is present. They do not decide what is correct, current, derived, or physically established.

## Repository maintenance

Current working surfaces include:

- `DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/` — exported conversations and associated source artifacts.
- `LIVE CONVOS/` — mutable/current conversation material; preserve its working character.
- `SAT_VISUALS/` — curated public-facing and working visual material.
- `tools/` — deterministic, auditable archive utilities.
- `indexes/` — generated structural catalogs, conversation chronology, date manifests, and machine-readable scan state.
- `ledgers/` — derived equation/dependency/citation records and point-of-use cross-links.

Yes. This is exactly the kind of continuity machinery that has been missing: instead of each new instance inheriting a compressed interpretation of the project, we can give it a minimum primary-source education and then continuously preserve your actual wording as the highest-value interpretive record.

I made the changes.

I replaced your placeholder in `INTERNAL/WORKING_INSTRUCTIONS.md` with the actual standing training requirement. It now points to the permanent Common prerequisite and explicitly says that no theory/formalization/solver/prediction/paper work happens before the required line-by-line reading is complete. Your “speed of time” clarification is now stated more precisely there and in `MINIMUM_THEORY_PREREQUISITES.md`:

\[
\text{speed of time is provisionally treated as basically fixed}
\]

and in the present construction that fixed rate manifests as

\[
\boxed{c=(\text{timesheet–filament intersection propagation})_w}.
\]

So we are no longer hedging away the fixed-speed premise. The provisional assumption is that the speed of time itself is basically fixed unless the model or evidence forces otherwise; the typing safeguard is that its \(c\) appears specifically as the \(w\)-component of the intersection propagation, not automatically as filament velocity, total tangent speed, phase speed, etc.

I also built `WORKSPACES/COMMON/TRAINING_SOURCE_MAP.md`. That is becoming the reading syllabus rather than stuffing everything into the minimum-prerequisite file.

A useful distinction has already emerged. The **latest project-state overviews** are the September reconstruction surfaces in `HsH/synthesis/`—especially `CURRENT_SYNTHESIS.md` and `LIVE_REBUILD_STATUS.md`. But those are our reconstructions, not substitutes for primary development material. fileciteturn191file0

For recent H(s)H developmental overviews, I have now positively located several much better training sources:

- `H(s)H 2026 STARTUP DOCS.txt` is extremely valuable. Its opening is you explaining the transition in your own words: the pure 4D nth-order nested-helical worldline programme, the Minkowski-map/control-case method, the rule of stripping inherited interpretations while preserving mapped facts, minimal geometric modification, holdout/cross-sector promotion, and then the need to lift the result from worldline to worldtube. fileciteturn210file0
- `H(s)H CLASSIC.txt` is definitely present and dates itself July 17, 2026, but it is heavily mixed with NotebookLM-generated material, so I’m treating it as development history rather than your voice wholesale. fileciteturn209file0
- `H(s)H BEGIN REVIEW.txt` is present and is a useful map of the worldtube-transition “hardware cabinet,” dimensional alternatives, stripped gears, interaction ideas, etc.—again mixed/generated and therefore something to audit rather than obey. fileciteturn212file0
- `SAT ALL TOGETHER SYNTHESIS.txt`, `SAT to H(s)H TRANSITION.txt`, `H(s)H_TIME_RESIDUALS.txt`, the REWORK/ARCHITECTING material, and the default all-purpose formalism are now on the syllabus as well.

I found the scratch material quite cleanly. The archive has:

`SCRATCH 1.txt` — begins **FROM SCRATCH**.  
`SCRATCH 2.txt` — begins **###. FROM SCRATCH 2**.  
`SCRATCH 4.txt` — begins **SAT FROM SCRATCH**.

And these are probably going to be unusually valuable for the training exercise.

`SCRATCH 1` and `SCRATCH 2` contain very direct statements from you about four observable dimensions being enough as the starting space, worldlines as the fundamental mapping tool, nested helices/superhelices, worldlines physically extending through the fourth dimension, and your insistence that the 4D extent need not be static. fileciteturn203file0L6-L18 fileciteturn204file0L10-L22

They also contain a historical formulation very close to the problem we're cleaning up now: you describe one dimension as expanding at the speed of light relative to the others, with our observed world being the current extent/front. fileciteturn203file0L18-L21 That gives us something much better than “Nathan says \(c\) means X”: we can actually reconstruct how your language about the speed of time, four-dimensional extension, intersection, and apparent motion evolved, and then place today's more precise formulation alongside it.

`SCRATCH 4` is almost tailor-made for the **pitfall** half of the curriculum. It contains the polished/generated claim that the timesheet is an expansion front at \(c\), then a total-four-velocity \(=c\) constraint, then later the specific moving-helix decomposition that helped produce the error we just caught. It even wanders into a 5D Kaluza–Klein construction despite the four-dimensional premise. fileciteturn205file0 In other words, we shouldn't throw that document away—we should teach from it: “Here is what happens when the assistant takes Nathan's geometric intuition and progressively conventionalizes it into machinery he did not actually specify.”

I also located the “Proper Dimensionality” material far enough to give it a stable search identity:

`project_sources/14-00-PROPER-DIMENSIONALITY-.txt`

It appears inside the archived `Reasoning with SAT-HSH Skill` working context. It includes SO(4), projection, worldline dimensionality, velocity decomposition, BV/AKSZ, 24-cell material, and a lot of 2026 imported mathematics. fileciteturn192file3L40-L40 fileciteturn192file4L50-L50 I have **not** yet found a durable GitHub path corresponding exactly to that local `project_sources/...` identifier, so the source map says precisely that rather than inventing a path. That document looks important enough to recover, but also contaminated enough that it should be read as an audit object, not a dimensionality bible.

Most importantly, I created:

`WORKSPACES/COMMON/NATHAN_VERIFIED_WORDS_COMPENDIUM.md`

This is deliberately stricter than an ordinary quote collection. An entry only goes into the verified section if the raw conversation metadata says it is a **user/Nathan message**. Each entry carries date, topic tags, exact conversation path, message ID/timestamp or landmark, exact wording, minimal context, historical status, and links to later corrections where applicable. Assistant paraphrases are forbidden. Style-matching is forbidden. Duplicate exports are deduplicated by conversation/message identity. Older statements stay even when you later correct them—the correction gets linked rather than rewriting history.

And I created the one automated instance you asked for: **Nathan Words Excavator**. It runs hourly. Its sole job during the standdown is provenance excavation—not theory construction. It systematically searches raw `DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS` and relevant live conversations, verifies that the message was yours, and appends your actual wording to the compendium with date/topic/source metadata. It prioritizes dimensionality, 4D thinking, speed of time, \(c\), \(w\), timesheet, intersection propagation, worldline/worldtube, rest and apparent motion, helix radius/pitch/arclength, projection/readout, UI, Whirligig, Spheres, Graticule, Hagalaz, finite core, interactions, metric, holonomy, methodology, and your explicit corrections.

It is specifically forbidden to “improve” what you said or turn assistant prose into Nathan prose. Ambiguous material goes into an unverified holding area.

One thing I think this will give us that we have never really had is a **diachronic Nathan layer**. Instead of asking “What does Nathan mean by time/worldline/timesheet?” and getting whichever compressed answer survived into memory, a future instance will be able to see something like:

> 2024 — early formulation  
> 2025 — explicit refinement  
> Feb. 2026 — Fundamental Intuitions Extended  
> June/July 2026 — worldline → worldtube transition  
> September 2026 — current correction  
> **relationship:** refinement / correction / displaced assumption

That is much closer to maintaining an actual scientific research programme than asking each fresh LLM to reconstruct your intent from whatever five documents it happens to retrieve.

And the source search has already demonstrated why it matters. The raw scratch material contains your actual 4D intuition sitting immediately next to assistant interpretations that subtly transform it. fileciteturn203file0L14-L21 The compendium gives us a way to keep those two things permanently separated.

1901: Address	What lives there	Typical occupants / landmarks	How the rest of physics sees it
1902: 1. Bedrock institutional physics	Experimentally nailed-down frameworks, precision measurement, established effective theories, mature phenomenology	LIGO, CERN experiments, precision AMO, condensed matter, nuclear physics, plasma physics, astrophysical surveys; people like Nergis Mavalvala on gravitational-wave detection and quantum measurement	“Physics.” Almost nobody argues about whether this belongs in the discipline. Mavalvala is about as downtown as one can get institutionally.
1903: 2. Mainstream research frontier	Unsettled questions approached with standard professional machinery	dark matter searches, neutrino physics, inflation, BSM phenomenology, quantum information, black holes, amplitudes, holography, string theory	Highly legitimate even where empirical confirmation is absent. Arguments are about which research program is promising, not whether participants are physicists.
1904: 3. Mainstream speculative theory	Deep extrapolation from established theory into inaccessible regimes	Witten, Maldacena, Arkani-Hamed; strings, holography, emergent spacetime, amplitudes	Sociologically mainstream, scientifically speculative. Witten and Maldacena are institutional-center figures even though quantum gravity remains unsolved.
1905: 4. Minority but fully legitimate programs	Programs whose premises differ substantially from the dominant route	Ashtekar/Rovelli/Smolin and LQG; Sorkin/causal sets; asymptotic safety; collapse models; Bohmian/foundations programs	“I may think you’re wrong, but of course this is physics.” Ashtekar and Smolin are obvious examples of deeply established insiders working away from the dominant string/QFT center.
1906: 5. Heterodox insider physics	Challenges to assumptions most physicists ordinarily take for granted	Milgrom/McGaugh on MOND-like gravity; ’t Hooft on deterministic foundations; Verlinde on emergent-gravity directions	Often controversial, sometimes strongly opposed, but entirely discussable in journals and seminars. ’t Hooft is the perfect reminder that heterodoxy and scientific stature are independent variables.
1907: 6. High-risk/iconoclastic insider territory	Ideas whose advocates have impeccable credentials but whose particular claims sit well outside consensus	Penrose’s more speculative cosmological/foundational programs; Avi Loeb’s extraterrestrial-technology interpretations of anomalous objects	The person is indisputably an insider; the specific claim may get eye-rolls, sharp criticism, or intense skepticism. Loeb, for example, was Harvard astronomy chair and runs the Galileo Project; his standing and the reception of particular ET interpretations are different questions.
1908: 7. Independent / para-academic fundamental-physics projects	Serious attempts conducted largely outside normal physics-group ecology	Stephen Wolfram’s Physics Project; Eric Weinstein’s Geometric Unity; some independent ToE projects	Not automatically pseudoscience. But they have much less uptake into the ordinary research metabolism: fewer independent groups, fewer graduate programs built around them, weaker peer-community feedback loops. Wolfram’s project is elaborate and technically developed; GU is explicitly presented as Weinstein’s independent unification attempt.
1909: 8. Pop-science / buzz-space	Real science mixed with extrapolation, entertainment, thumbnails, hype cycles and “physics may be broken” narratives	YouTube, podcasts, magazine headlines, futurism, quantum-consciousness stories, wormhole headlines, “new force” stories	Quality ranges from excellent to awful. This is a media ecosystem, not a scientific category. Good physicists routinely appear here.
1910: 9. Actual fringe	Programs substantially disconnected from accumulated constraint, professional correction mechanisms or basic mathematics	anti-relativity systems, perpetual-motion/free-energy schemes, numerological ToEs, “Einstein was wrong and academia suppresses me,” Electric-Universe-like ecosystems	Here the problem is usually not merely an unconventional premise. It is failure to absorb existing constraints, lack of meaningful independent criticism, moving goalposts, or inability to reproduce established physics.
1911: 10. Far fringe / physics-shaped belief system	Physics vocabulary without functioning scientific discipline	conspiratorial cosmologies, magical-energy systems, claims immunized against falsification	The opposite pole from professional physics.
1912: 
1913: The center of gravity of actual physics is around 1–3, not because everybody believes string theory or ΛCDM is sacred, but because this is where the enormous institutional apparatus of experiment, calculation, peer criticism, instrumentation and trained specialists lives.
1914: 
1915: The numerical majority of working physicists are also much less philosophically dramatic than the public picture suggests. A huge share of physics is materials, optics, semiconductors, medical physics, fluid/plasma work, instrumentation, condensed matter, accelerator work, computational physics, geophysics, photonics, quantum devices, metrology, and so forth. “What is spacetime?” occupies a much bigger percentage of YouTube physics than of physicists’ payrolls.
1916: 
1917: Now zoom in: the insiders’ spectrum
1918: 
1919: Here I would draw the road from “bedrock” → “mainstream frontier” → “recognized alternative” → “heterodox but absolutely one of us” → “you can give this seminar, but expect blood on the floor.”
1920: 
1921: The positions below are about the research stance, not personal quality:
1922: 
1923: Insider zone	Representative people	What they represent
1924: Bedrock / calibration standard	Nergis Mavalvala, Rainer Weiss, major CERN/LIGO/precision-measurement leadership	You are testing known physical frameworks or extracting genuinely new phenomena from instruments. Argument happens inside tight empirical constraints. Mavalvala’s research is gravitational-wave detection and quantum measurement science.
1925: Mainstream theory establishment	Edward Witten, Juan Maldacena	Extremely speculative subject matter, but the mathematical and institutional center of high-energy theory. Witten helped make string theory and its mathematical descendants central research subjects; Maldacena’s work sits at QFT/string/quantum-gravity/holography.
1926: Aggressive mainstream frontier	Nima Arkani-Hamed	Will happily question whether the usual formulation is the right formulation, but does so from inside elite particle theory with direct concern for experiments. His amplitudes work is a good example: radically reformulating calculation without leaving the professional center. IAS hosted the 2024 Amplitudes conference under his co-organization.
1927: Established alternative program	Abhay Ashtekar, Carlo Rovelli, Lee Smolin, Rafael Sorkin	“The dominant route to quantum gravity may be wrong; here is another mature mathematical program.” Nobody serious needs to pretend LQG or causal sets are consensus to recognize them as normal theoretical physics. Perimeter institutionalizes exactly this pluralism.
1928: Heterodox insider	Mordehai Milgrom, Stacy McGaugh, Gerard ’t Hooft, Erik Verlinde	Challenges something close to the default explanatory picture: dark matter via modified dynamics; fundamental probabilism via determinism; gravity as emergent. They can be strongly disagreed with without being socially or methodologically outside physics. ’t Hooft is a Nobel laureate whose present work explicitly investigates deterministic quantum mechanics.
1929: Prestige-supported iconoclast	Roger Penrose, Avi Loeb	The CV buys you enormous latitude to explore unusual possibilities—but not automatic assent. Penrose can be simultaneously one of the architects of modern relativistic black-hole theory and advocate much more contentious ideas elsewhere.
1930: Conference-border / external research ecosystem	Wolfram Physics Project; some independent unification programs	Technically literate work with some real mathematical substance, but not deeply integr
...[truncated]...
ponents of its theoretical-physics program.
1936: 
1937: Conversely, MOND sounds modest—change one force law at low acceleration—but sociologically it sits farther from the consensus cosmological model than holography does from mainstream high-energy theory. McGaugh nevertheless chairs an astronomy department and works directly on galaxy dynamics and the mass-discrepancy problem.
1938: 
1939: And ’t Hooft is the great spectrum-breaker. If an unknown independent researcher said “quantum mechanics may emerge from an underlying deterministic system,” many physicists would immediately suspect crank territory. When Gerard ’t Hooft says it, it is a minority foundational research program pursued by somebody whose earlier work helped establish the quantum consistency of the Standard Model. The proposition does not become true because of his CV; the CV tells you that “heterodox claim” and “fringe scientist” are not synonyms.
1940: 
1941: Where the famous public faces actually live
1942: 
1943: This is where the map gets amusing.
1944: 
1945: Sean Carroll is not principally “a science communicator who knows physics.” He is an academic foundational theorist working on quantum mechanics, spacetime, cosmology, emergence and entropy who also happens to have a large public platform. On the insider map he is around mainstream-frontier/foundations territory; his public persona is much closer to consensus exposition than some of the questions he researches.
1946: 
1947: Sabine Hossenfelder is almost the reverse public archetype: a trained foundations physicist with a substantial publication record whose public niche is aggressive criticism of hype, fashionable methodology, and weak evidentiary claims. Her own site describes more than 80 research papers in cosmology, quantum foundations and particle physics and now identifies her prominently as physicist/author/content creator. On the public spectrum she can sound much farther from the establishment than her actual technical provenance warrants.
1948: 
1949: Brian Greene is a bona fide string theorist whose public work occupies clean science communication and popular science. His research identity is closer to Witten/Maldacena territory than most viewers of The Elegant Universe probably realize.
1950: 
1951: Brian Cox came out of experimental particle physics and is largely a mainstream-consensus public interpreter. His public profile sits closer to “tour guide to the downtown” than “founder of a heterodox district.”
1952: 
1953: Neil deGrasse Tyson is a legitimate astrophysicist and institutional science communicator, but he is not a useful marker for the cutting edge of fundamental-theory factional politics. His public role is much more “explain the scientific consensus and scientific worldview.”
1954: 
1955: Katie Mack and Becky Smethurst are useful examples of current-research-trained communicators: their public material largely gives outsiders a pretty honest view of mainstream cosmology/astrophysics without pretending the field is more settled than it is.
1956: 
1957: Michio Kaku is the interesting boundary case. His professional ancestry is real theoretical physics/string-field work, while his media persona ranges much further into futurism and highly extrapolative material. If you only see the public persona, you would place him much farther toward “buzz-space” than his academic provenance alone would suggest.
1958: 
1959: Roger Penrose barely fits the usual communicator category at all. He is one of the bedrock figures of mathematical relativity who also occupies some of the field’s most eccentric neighborhoods. This makes him an excellent demonstration that the spectrum is about claims, not people.
1960: 
1961: Some towny knowledge that matters
1962: 
1963: There are several unwritten rules an outsider can easily miss.
1964: 
1965: First, physicists tolerate astonishing speculative freedom downstream of competence. You can talk about emergent spacetime, extra dimensions, multiverses, deterministic subquantum dynamics, cyclic cosmology, causal sets or modified gravity and remain completely respectable if you know the existing theory cold, formulate the departure precisely, engage the literature, and accept constraints.
1966: 
1967: Second, the real taboo is usually not “weird idea.” It is not knowing what has already been ruled out. A strange proposal with a careful EFT limit and a constraint table gets a hearing. A modest-sounding proposal that violates Lorentz tests, conservation law, known scattering data, or dimensional consistency and does not notice will rapidly get sorted into a different social category.
1968: 
1969: Third, credentials buy attention, not truth. Penrose can get a room for a wild idea because everyone knows he can do the conventional calculation. The wild idea still gets attacked. A Nobel Prize allows ’t Hooft to make determinism a serious seminar topic; it does not make determinism consensus.
1970: 
1971: Fourth, the theoretical community is substantially less monolithic than “mainstream physics” sounds. Even inside quantum gravity, an institution like Perimeter deliberately houses LQG, spin foams, group field theory, matrix models, CDT, asymptotic safety, causal sets and string-related approaches simultaneously. The insider argument is often not orthodoxy versus heresy. It is which kind of heresy has earned enough mathematical and empirical discipline to become a research program.
1972: 
1973: Fifth, there is a big gulf between “not consensus” and “nobody is working on this.” MOND is not the cosmological consensus. It is nevertheless a real research literature. LQG is not the dominant quantum-gravity program. It is nevertheless a professional research community. Deterministic quantum mechanics is not the standard interpretation. A Nobel laureate nevertheless publishes on it.
1974: 
1975: Sixth, the farthest acceptable insider position is not fixed. A technique can migrate. Twistors were once seen by many theorists as an elegant curiosity; Witten’s use of them in scattering theory helped move them much closer to the mainstream. Yesterday’s weird mathematics can become tomorrow’s standard machinery without the underlying grand theory that motivated it ever winning.
1976: 
1977: And that, I think, is the most useful way to picture the town:
1978: 
1979: The center is not “people with conventional ideas.” The center is people embedded in powerful correction mechanisms.
1980: 
1981: The further outward you go, the less the decisive issue becomes how strange is the proposition? and the more it becomes how much independent constraint, technical competence, reproducibility, literature contact, adversarial feedback, and institutional cross-checking surrounds it?
1982: 
1983: That distinction is going to matter a great deal when we eventually ask where SAT sits on this map, because on the content axis several SAT ideas have analogues in perfectly respectable minority neighborhoods, while on the social-validation axis SAT is presently an independent research program with essentially none of the institutional error-correction that protects even very heterodox insider physics. Those are two completely different measurements.
1984: 
1985: Alright, now I want you to tell me how 2024 physics--mainstream/professional/academic/corporate/experimental/theoretical ranks on our SATity fingerprint analysis. Clean yea/nea or skip. For two patients, I want you to fingerprint them with our SAT scale, first the real physics core as one specimen, then as a second specimen the broader mainstream but poppy/casual totality of everyone who's interested in physics... treating all of respectable physics as a single, albiet diverse consensus theory. Treating all of the wide world fo general phys-ish community as another. And then for the third, the wild super-physicsy but super not-acceptable fringe. Try to keep your rankings highly compressed. Rank by the criteria as given, but give output as single or few-word labels so we can fit this all in one overview packet.

1987: Here's your fingerprint criteria for reference.
